issues.legal_issue: A commissioner conducting a statutory survey of endowment properties may inquire whether a disputed property is an endowment property.
material_facts: A commissioner was appointed to survey existing wakf properties.
A claimant alleged that a building was wakf property and that its transfer by the mutawalli was invalid.
The purchasers disputed that the building was wakf property and challenged the commissioner’s jurisdiction to inquire into its status.
After receiving evidence, the commissioner reported that the building was wakf property, and the Board included it in the published list.
issues.conclusion: The commissioner acted within jurisdiction in determining that the disputed property was wakf property, and the Board was justified in including it in the list.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4(1), 4(3), and 4(4) of the Wakf Act, 1954, the power to survey wakf properties necessarily includes inquiry into whether a wakf exists and whether disputed property is wakf property; the commissioner’s inquiry has a quasi-judicial character for persons within the scope of section 6(1). Section 4(5) concerns resolving whether a wakf is Shia or Sunni by reference to the deed where it clearly indicates its nature; it does not limit inquiry into whether the property is wakf property. Reading sections 4, 5, and 6 together supports this construction. The Court also applied the principle in Crawford v. Spooner that a court cannot repair defective statutory wording, while reconciling provisions to give effect to the statute.

predicates.statutory_endowment_survey: The proceeding involves a commissioner appointed to survey existing religious endowment properties.
predicates.disputed_property_status: A person disputes whether a particular property is part of the religious endowment.
predicates.commissioner_has_investigatory_powers: The commissioner is empowered to investigate matters relevant to the survey using court-like evidence-gathering powers.

issues.definition: When a property’s status is disputed during a statutory endowment survey and the commissioner has investigatory powers, the commissioner may determine its endowment status as part of that survey.

issues.legal_issue: A non-Muslim stranger in possession of property is not bound by the special limitation period or the finality of a published wakf list when challenging the property’s inclusion.
material_facts: The purchasers were non-Muslims who claimed possession and title to the building as mortgagees and purchasers.
The Board included the building in its published list of wakfs.
The purchasers were strangers to the wakf, rather than the Board, a mutawalli, or persons interested in the wakf as defined by the Act.
They had not brought a suit within the period specified in section 6(1).
issues.conclusion: The published list was not final and conclusive against the purchasers, and their failure to sue within the period in section 6(1) did not bar them from challenging the list or bringing a suit to establish their title.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(h), 6(1), and 6(4) of the Wakf Act, 1954, the word “therein” in “any person interested therein” refers to a person interested in the wakf, not any person interested in the property. The special limitation rule and the finality of the list apply to the Board, the mutawalli, and persons interested in the wakf, not to a non-Muslim stranger in possession. The Court relied on Sirajul Hag Khan v. The Sunni Central Board of Wakf, U.P., and agreed with the construction that section 6 confines the dispute to those connected with the wakf.

rule.if: wakf_list_challenge_limitation_proceeding and claimant_is_non_muslim_stranger and claimant_possesses_property and claimant_not_interested_in_wakf

predicates.wakf_list_challenge_limitation_proceedin: The proceeding concerns a challenge to a property’s inclusion in a published list of wakfs and the limitation applicable to that challenge.
predicates.claimant_is_non_muslim_stranger: The claimant is a non-Muslim who is neither the Board, the mutawalli, nor a person connected with the wakf.
predicates.claimant_possesses_property: The claimant is in possession of the property included in the list.
predicates.claimant_not_interested_in_wakf: The claimant is not a person entitled to benefits from the wakf or otherwise within the statutory description of a person interested in it.

issues.definition: When a non-Muslim stranger in possession who is not interested in the wakf challenges inclusion of the property in the wakf list, the special limitation bar and list finality do not bind that claimant.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not decide the applicability of statutory registration or recovery powers, or grant relief based on that determination, when the issue was not raised or was unnecessary to resolve.
material_facts: The purchasers’ writ petition challenged the commissioner’s inquiry and the inclusion of the property in the wakf list.
The High Court restrained the Board from registering the property and from dispossessing the purchasers except through a civil suit, based on its view of the Board’s statutory powers.
The Supreme Court found that no relief concerning the Board’s registration power had been sought and that the applicability of the recovery provision did not arise for consideration.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s direction restraining the Board from registering the property or dispossessing the purchasers, and left the applicability of those statutory powers open.
issues.legal_principle: The Court did not decide the scope of sections 27 and 36B of the Wakf Act, 1954. It held that the High Court’s observations on section 27 were unnecessary because no relief concerning action under that section had been sought, and that it was unnecessary to decide whether section 36B applied on the facts. The resulting direction, which rested on assumptions about those provisions, therefore could not stand.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_order: The proceeding is an appeal from a court order resolving a writ petition.
predicates.statutory_power_issue_not_raised_or_unne: The applicability of an authority’s statutory power was not raised for relief or was unnecessary to decide the dispute.
predicates.lower_court_restrained_authority_based_o: The lower court restrained the authority based on its view of the unraised or unnecessary statutory-power issue.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a writ order, if the lower court restrained an authority based on a statutory-power issue that was not raised or was unnecessary to decide, the restraint is set aside and that issue remains open.
